# Run time: 2026-11-05T03:29:54.440324-05:00

# Overview

Costco Wholesale Corporation operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites based on the concept that "offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products in a wide range of categories will produce high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover" (10-k.txt:724). The company began operations in 1983 in Seattle, Washington, and as of August 30, 2026, operated 939 warehouses worldwide (10-k.txt:721). The business model relies on operating profitably at "significantly lower gross margins (net sales less merchandise costs) than most other retailers" by leveraging volume purchasing, efficient distribution, and reduced handling in no-frills, self-service facilities (10-k.txt:724).

The company’s revenue is derived from net sales and membership fees. For the fiscal year ended August 30, 2026, net sales increased 10% to $297,247 million, and membership fee revenue increased 11% to $5,907 million (10-k.txt:1032, 10-k.txt:1036). The membership format is described as "integral to our business and profitability," designed to reinforce member loyalty and provide continuing fee revenue (10-k.txt:1018). At the end of 2026, the company had 84,100 thousand paid members and 66,300 thousand household cards, totaling 150,400 thousand cardholders (10-k.txt:763-765). Executive members, who pay an additional annual fee and earn a reward generally of 2% on qualified purchases, represented 42,300 thousand of total paid members in 2026 (10-k.txt:769).

The company’s merchandise categories include core merchandise (foods and sundries, non-foods, fresh foods), warehouse ancillary services (gasoline, pharmacy, food court, optical, hearing aids, and tire installation), and other businesses (e-commerce, business centers, travel, and other) (10-k.txt:735-750). Gasoline operations are a significant traffic driver, with 774 gas stations operated at the end of 2026, representing 11% of total net sales (10-k.txt:751). Digitally-enabled sales, which include sales initiated through a digital device and Costco Travel, represented 11% of total net sales in 2026 (10-k.txt:754).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Costco’s competitive position is built on its ability to provide "a broad range of high-quality merchandise at prices we believe are consistently lower than elsewhere" (10-k.txt:731). The company maintains a limited assortment, carrying "less than 4,000 active stock keeping units (SKUs) per warehouse in our core warehouse business, significantly less than other broadline retailers" (10-k.txt:731). This limited selection allows for high inventory turnover and rapid sales, enabling the company to "often sell inventory before we are required to pay for it, even while taking advantage of early payment discounts" (10-k.txt:724).

The company acknowledges that competition is "vigorous and widespread, across a wide range of global, national, and regional wholesalers and retailers, including those with e-commerce operations" (10-k.txt:1010). To maintain its position, Costco focuses on "pricing authority" – consistently providing the most competitive values – rather than maximizing prices in the short term (10-k.txt:1011). The company’s strategy includes working with suppliers to share cost increases, sourcing in countries where items are sold, and increasing the penetration of private-label items (10-k.txt:1010-1011).

Growth is driven by comparable sales growth, which is achieved through "increasing shopping frequency from new and existing members and the amount they spend on each visit (average ticket)" (10-k.txt:1010). For the fiscal year 2026, total company comparable sales increased 8.4% on an adjusted basis, excluding the impacts from changes in gasoline prices and foreign exchange (exhibit-99-1.txt:17). The company also achieves net sales growth by opening new warehouses; in 2026, it opened 28 new warehouses, including three relocations, for a total of 25 net new warehouses (10-k.txt:1030). The company notes that as its warehouse base grows, "available and desirable sites become more difficult to secure, square footage growth becomes a comparatively less substantial component of growth" (10-k.txt:1017).

The company’s financial performance is sensitive to economic conditions, inflation, and competition. The MD&A states that "the health of the economies in which we do business, including the effects of inflation or deflation, especially the United States" is a substantial factor in net sales growth (10-k.txt:1010). Additionally, "government actions in various countries relating to tariffs affect the costs of some of our merchandise," with higher tariffs more likely to adversely impact results (10-k.txt:1015).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

The company’s future growth strategy continues to focus on expanding its warehouse base, particularly in international markets where "the rate of square footage growth is generally higher... due to the smaller base in those markets, and we expect that to continue" (10-k.txt:1017). The company also aims to increase the penetration of Executive memberships and sustain high renewal rates, which "materially influences our profitability" (10-k.txt:1018). The worldwide renewal rate was 89.8% at the end of 2026 (10-k.txt:770).

A key strategic focus is the expansion of digitally-enabled sales, which grew 20.9% on an adjusted basis for the fiscal year 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:18). The company continues to invest in e-commerce operations and logistics to support this growth, noting that "our e-commerce operations ship merchandise through our depots and logistics operations, as well as through drop-ship and other delivery arrangements with our suppliers" (10-k.txt:728).

The company faces ongoing challenges related to labor costs and employee retention. It employs 355,000 employees worldwide, with approximately 95% employed in membership warehouses and distribution channels (10-k.txt:776). The company’s philosophy is to maintain compensation levels "better than the industry average for much of our workforce" to reduce turnover and increase productivity, acknowledging that "modest changes in various items in the consolidated statements of income, particularly merchandise costs and SG&A expenses, can have substantial impacts on net income" due to the business’s low margins (10-k.txt:1019).

The filing does not establish a claim regarding specific future warehouse opening targets beyond the expectation that international square footage growth will continue at a higher rate than domestic growth (10-k.txt:1017). The filing does not establish a claim regarding specific future membership fee increases beyond the historical trend of fee increases contributing to revenue growth (10-k.txt:1036). The filing does not establish a claim regarding specific future private-label product launches beyond the general strategy of increasing private-label penetration (10-k.txt:1010).

## Investment Recommendation

**Recommendation:** Hold

**Thesis:** Costco Wholesale Corporation demonstrates strong operational fundamentals, including 10.14% annual revenue growth and a 28.40% return on average equity for the fiscal year ended August 30, 2026. However, the stock trades at a premium valuation of 47.79x FY-EPS, which is high relative to the company's 3.85% operating margin. While the business model is robust, the lack of a clear valuation benchmark against peers that justifies this premium multiple, combined with the high entry price, suggests a neutral stance.

**Deciding Number:** 47.79x FY-EPS (Price-to-Earnings Ratio)

**Citation:** The 47.79x FY-EPS is derived from the Financial Analyst output, calculated as $992.13 (price on 2026-10-27) divided by $20.76 (FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS). The period is FY2026 (2025-09-01 to 2026-08-30).

**Limitation:** The supplied analysis lacks a comprehensive valuation benchmark (such as a peer-adjusted P/E multiple or intrinsic value model) to definitively determine if the current 47.79x multiple is overvalued or fairly priced relative to growth expectations. Therefore, a Hold recommendation is preferred to avoid potential overpayment for earnings.

When combined with the operating efficiencies achieved by volume purchasing, efficient distribution and reduced handling of merchandise in no-frills, self-service warehouse facilities, these volumes and turnover enable us to operate profitably at significantly lower gross margins (net sales less merchandise costs) than most other retailers. We often sell inventory before we are required to pay for it, even while taking advantage of early payment discounts.

cited_filing_lines.report_sentence: The membership format is described as "integral to our business and profitability," designed to reinforce member loyalty and provide continuing fee revenue
cited_filing_lines.source_line: The membership format is integral to our business and profitability. This format is designed to reinforce member loyalty and provide continuing fee revenue. The extent to which we achieve growth in our membership base, increase the penetration of Executive memberships, and sustain high renewal rates materially influences our profitability. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our paid-membership growth rate may be adversely impacted when warehouse openings occur in existing markets as compared to new markets. Our worldwide renewal rate is adversely impacted by membership growth in certain international markets and a higher penetration of memberships sold online, including through digital membership promotions, which renew at a slightly lower rate on average.

cited_filing_lines.report_sentence: Executive members, who pay an additional annual fee and earn a reward generally of 2% on qualified purchases, represented 42,300 thousand of total paid members in 2026
cited_filing_lines.source_line: Paid members, in most countries, are eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership for an additional annual fee. These members earn an Executive reward, generally 2% on qualified purchases, subject to an annual maximum value, redeemable at Costco warehouses. Executive members represented 42,300, 38,700, and 35,400 of total paid members in 2026, 2025, and 2024. The penetration of sales to Executive members represented approximately 75.2% of worldwide net sales in 2026.

cited_filing_lines.report_sentence: Gasoline operations are a significant traffic driver, with 774 gas stations operated at the end of 2026, representing 11% of total net sales
cited_filing_lines.source_line: Warehouse ancillary operate primarily within, next to or near our warehouses, encouraging more frequent shopping. The number of warehouses with gas stations varies significantly by country. We operated 774 gas stations at the end of 2026. Our gasoline business represented 11% of total net sales in 2026.

cited_filing_lines.report_sentence: Digitally-enabled sales, which include sales initiated through a digital device and Costco Travel, represented 11% of total net sales in 2026
cited_filing_lines.source_line: Our other businesses sell products and services that largely complement our warehouse operations. Our business centers carry items tailored for food services, convenience stores, and offices, and offer walk-in shopping and deliveries. Business centers are included in our total warehouse count. Our e-commerce operations give members convenience and a broader selection of goods and services. Costco Travel offers vacation packages, car rentals, cruises and other travel products exclusively for Costco members in varying degrees in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and Australia. Digitally-enabled sales, which represents sales that are initiated through a digital device, whether fulfilled through a warehouse or distribution center, as well as Costco Travel, represented 11% of total net sales in 2026.

cited_filing_lines.report_sentence:
# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Costco’s competitive position is built on its ability to provide "a broad range of high-quality merchandise at prices we believe are consistently lower than elsewhere"
cited_filing_lines.source_line: Our strategy is to provide our members with a broad range of high-quality merchandise at prices we believe are consistently lower than elsewhere. We seek to limit most items to fast-selling models, sizes, and colors. We carry less than 4,000 active stock keeping units (SKUs) per warehouse in our core warehouse business, significantly less than other broadline retailers. We average from 9,000 to 11,000 SKUs online, some of which are available in our warehouses. Many consumable products are offered for sale in case, carton, or multiple-pack quantities only.

cited_filing_lines.report_sentence: The company acknowledges that competition is "vigorous and widespread, across a wide range of global, national, and regional wholesalers and retailers, including those with e-commerce operations"
cited_filing_lines.source_line: We believe that the most important driver of our profitability is increasing net sales, particularly comparable sales. Net sales includes our core merchandise categories (foods and sundries, non-foods, and fresh foods), warehouse ancillary (gasoline, pharmacy, food court, optical, hearing aids, and tire installation), and other businesses (e-commerce, business centers, travel, and other). E-commerce and business center sales are allocated to the appropriate merchandise categories in the Net Sales discussion. The Executive reward earned by our Executive members reduces net sales and is allocated to the category in which the reward is generated (core merchandise categories, warehouse ancillary, and other businesses). Comparable sales is defined as net sales from warehouses operating for more than one year, including remodels, relocations, and expansions. Digitally-enabled comparable sales is defined as sales initiated through a digital device, whether fulfilled through a warehouse, distribution center, or Costco Travel, operating for more than one year. Comparable sales metrics are intended as supplemental information and are not a substitute for net sales presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP) and should be reviewed in conjunction with results reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Comparable sales growth is achieved through increasing shopping frequency from new and existing members and the amount they spend on each visit (average ticket). Sales comparisons can also be particularly influenced by certain factors that are beyond our control: fluctuations in currency exchange rates (with respect to our international operations) and inflation or deflation in the cost of gasoline and associated competitive conditions. The higher our comparable sales exclusive of these items, the more we can leverage our selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses, reducing them as a percentage of sales and enhancing profitability. Generating comparable sales growth is foremost a question of making available the right merchandise at the right prices, a skill that we believe we have repeatedly demonstrated over the long-term. Another substantial factor in net sales growth is the health of the economies in which we do business, including the effects of inflation or deflation, especially the United States. Net sales growth and gross margins are also impacted by competition, which is vigorous and widespread, across a wide range of global, national, and regional wholesalers and retailers, including those with e-commerce operations. While we cannot control or reliably predict general economic health or changes in competition, we believe that we have been successful, historically, in adapting our business to these changes, such as through adjustments to our pricing and merchandise mix, including increasing the penetration of our private-label items, and through online offerings.

cited_filing_lines.report_sentence: To maintain its position, Costco focuses on "pricing authority" – consistently providing the most competitive values – rather than maximizing prices in the short term

cited_filing_lines.source_line: Our member renewal rate was 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026. This rate is a trailing calculation that captures renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Memberships that have an expiration date in the six months prior to the end of our reporting period are excluded from this calculation, regardless of whether or not they have been renewed. Although most members renew prior to expiration, the vast majority of those who renew late do so within six months of expiration. The timing of renewal after expiration is impacted by a variety of factors, such as warehouse openings and promotional activity.

cited_filing_lines.report_sentence: The company’s philosophy is to maintain compensation levels "better than the industry average for much of our workforce" to reduce turnover and increase productivity, acknowledging that "modest changes in various items in the consolidated statements of income, particularly merchandise costs and SG&A expenses, can have substantial impacts on net income" due to the business’s low margins
cited_filing_lines.source_line: Our financial performance depends heavily on controlling costs. While we believe that we have achieved successes in this area, some significant costs are partially outside our control, particularly health care and utility expenses. With respect to the compensation of our employees, our philosophy is not to seek to minimize their wages and benefits. Rather, we believe that achieving our longer-term objectives of reducing employee turnover, increasing productivity, and enhancing employee satisfaction requires maintaining compensation levels that are better than the industry average for much of our workforce. This may cause us, for example, to absorb costs that other employers might seek to pass through to their workforces. Because our business operates on very low margins, modest changes in various items in the consolidated statements of income, particularly merchandise costs and SG&A expenses, can have substantial impacts on net income.
